welcome: Welcome, Commander. Your mission clock has started. Watch for an alert, then press Tab to open Luna.
s1: Oh no! A warning light is flashing! Something might be wrong with the landing system. We are approaching the Moon and preparing to land at Fra Mauro. What do you do?
s1_a: Mission Control found the problem! The warning is fixed, but you used some time. Good communication, Commander. We can continue the descent.
s1_b: The warning is still flashing! Mission Control fixes it, but you have lost more time. Next time, report a warning promptly. We can now continue.
s1_c: Your crew is safe! You stopped the landing. We will return to lunar orbit without reaching the surface. Protecting the crew is always a valid decision.
s2: Oh no! The radar is not working! You cannot see how far you are from the Moon's surface. The landing has started. What do you do?
s2_a: The radar is working again! You used some time troubleshooting it. Reliable height data is restored. We can approach the landing area.
s2_b: The backup sensor shows your height, but it uses extra power. I have marked the backup height sensor active. We can approach the landing area.
s2_c: You can see the Moon's surface, but you do not know exactly how high you are. Visual observation does not replace reliable height data. Continuing to land will be an unsafe attempt in this simulation.
s3: Oh no! There are large rocks in the landing area, and your fuel is running low! We are very close to the Moon. Look through the windows and choose your landing plan.
s3_a: The lights help you see the rocks better, but you use extra power. The lights are now on. You still need to choose where to land: between the rocks, or in the clear area farther away.
s3_b: You save fuel, but the spaceship lands too close to the rocks. The landing is dangerous. Let us review the result of this unsafe landing attempt.
s3_c: You find a clear place to land, but you use more fuel to reach it. Stand by for the final descent. I am guiding the ship toward the clear area.
descent: Final descent in progress. Watch the landing site through the windows. The terrain is coming closer. Stand by for touchdown.
secret: Touchdown confirmed! Outstanding work, Commander. You made safe decisions and preserved enough fuel, power, and time. You unlocked the secret ending: Fra Mauro Pathfinder.
normal: Touchdown confirmed. Your crew has landed safely at Fra Mauro. This is the good ending. Review the resource costs and your decisions, then try again to earn the secret ending.
bad_height: Landing attempt stopped. We did not have reliable height data. This is the bad ending. Next time, restore the radar or use the backup height sensor before committing to a landing.
bad_rocks: Unsafe touchdown. The ship came down dangerously close to the rocks. This is the bad ending. A clear landing zone is worth the extra fuel when the crew's safety is at stake.
bad_resource: The landing attempt has run out of a required resource. This is the bad ending. Review your fuel, power, and mission-time budget before trying again.
safe: Safe abort complete. Your crew is secure in lunar orbit. This is the safe ending. You did not land, but everyone is protected. You can restart the training when you are ready.
briefing: Apollo 14 landed at Fra Mauro on February fifth, nineteen seventy-one. The real mission faced an abort-switch fault and a landing-radar problem. Our resource costs and branching choices are game simulations. The lunar ground shown here also uses a crop of L R O camera terrain data.
mission_alert: Commander, a new mission needs your attention. Press Tab to open Luna.
task_1a: Walk to the highlighted communications console on the left. Use the Mission Control uplink switch, marked S band. Aim at it and press E to ask for help.
task_1b: Go to the front dashboard. Press the highlighted master caution light to acknowledge the warning. We will wait for a system recheck.
task_recheck_done: The warning is still flashing. Walk to the highlighted S band uplink on the left communications console and press E to call Mission Control.
task_1c: Go to the flight control panel beside the rear door. Press the red abort button to stop the landing and return the crew to orbit.
task_2a: Walk to the sensor console on the right. Switch the highlighted radar off, then switch it back on to test the settings.
task_radar_on: Radar power is off. Press E on the radar switch again to turn it on and retest.
task_2b: Walk to the highlighted sensor console on the right. Find the backup height sensor, marked LIDAR, and press E to switch it on. I will read the height after you activate it.
task_2c: Walk to the highlighted port window at the front left. Look through the glass and press E at the observation marker to report what you see.
task_3a: Look up at the overhead panel. Find the highlighted exterior lights switch and press E to turn on the landing lights.
task_3b: Go to the flight control panel beside the rear door. Press the amber commit button to select the landing site between the rocks.
task_3c: Go to the flight control panel beside the rear door. Press the cyan divert button to select the clear landing zone farther away.
